DEF F := /work/putnam_2023_b4.lean
GOAL replace the sorry in F with a kernel-checked proof of IsLeast {T | ...} 29.
FACT F <- tool: statement has one sorry; the hypotheses faithfully encode the problem (tne is an open set, so derivWithin is deriv there).
HYP answer 29 is least T.
REFUTER HYP: take the best configuration by hand and check the lower bound.
PLAN 1: model the dynamics. Each phase k resets f' to 0 at t_k, so on a gap of length d_k f gains (k+1)d_k^2/2. The final phase has acceleration n+1.
INFER f(t0+T) - 1/2 = sum_{k<n} (k+1)d_k^2/2 + (n+1)tau^2/2 with T = sum d_k + tau, and d_k >= 1.
CHECK 1 <- REFUTER HYP: with all d_k = 1, minimise n + sqrt(2(2022.5 - n(n+1)/4)/(n+1)) over n.
RESULT 1: n=8 gives T≈29.11; n=9 gives tau=20 exactly and T=29; n=10 gives T≈29.04. So the minimum is 29 at n=9, which supports the answer.
STATE F live; HYP answer 29 supported by hand computation; no Lean code yet.
GIVEUP <- the Lean proof needs two substantial developments, and I have not built either:
- Witness: ts k = k (for k ≤ 9), f piecewise quadratic with 1 + k pieces. Each iteratedDerivWithin 2 / derivWithin / ContDiffOn fact on tne must be proven by hand, including the right-limit conditions at each ts k.
- Lower bound: for an arbitrary n and arbitrary gaps ≥ 1, show f(t0+s) - 1/2 ≤ φ(s) for an explicit comparison function φ with φ(29) = 2022.5. This needs an induction over phases, extracting derivative facts from derivWithin on the open set tne, and integrating piecewise.

I give up. I did not produce a compiling proof, so I have not modified /work/putnam_2023_b4.lean. The value 29 is supported by my hand computation above, but that is not Lean evidence.
